key_insight: SLIM learns to remove redundant material from 3D lattices in a single forward prediction while approximately preserving homogenized elasticity.
engineering_relevance: The model enables rapid refinement of existing lattice designs without running topology optimization or homogenization analysis for each prediction.
method: Train a dual-octree implicit network to predict lightweight lattice signed-distance fields.
Use training pairs generated by property-constrained topology optimization.
Penalize estimated stiffness changes using target-based homogenization sensitivities.
evidence_signal: On 906 held-out lattices, SLIM achieved 15.90% mean relative volume-fraction reduction, 90.51% lightweighting success, and 0.636% mean normalized aggregate TO-target error, with generation taking approximately 0.5 s versus 2516.0 s for direct topology optimization.
watch_item: Training requires optimized targets and homogenization sensitivities; performance beyond the evaluated lattice distribution remains unestablished.
paper_title: SLIM: Learning an Operator for Material-Efficient 3D Lattice Refinement
